title: Architecture Gap Analysis — MCP Layer + Orchestrator (2026-05-03)
summary: Detailed analysis of structural divergence between stdio MCP server and HTTP bridge, orchestrator stub functions, and VSCode extension incomplete context layer. Phase 2 package extraction resolves all identified drift risks.
key_findings: Tool surface divergence: mcp-server.js exposes 18 tools; mcp-http-bridge.mjs exposes 20 (adds gitmcp_search, integrate_mcp_tool, deploy_production)
Persona enrichment gap: HTTP bridge runs enrichAgentsWithPersonas() mapping persona→model before CrewAI invocation; stdio server does not — callers must inject model manually
Schema mismatch in run_factory_mission: stdio server takes flat args (project, objective, persona); HTTP bridge takes context object (sessionId, task, memory, constraints, metadata)
Three duplicate files create drift risk: scripts/mcp-server.js (8 tools, stale), core/mcp-http-bridge.mjs (character-for-character copy of apps/api/ version)
Worf reflection score parse fallback: if regex fails, score defaults to 10 — mission passes without actual quality audit (core/orchestrator.js line ~361)
VSCode stubs: context.ts (450 bytes), executor.ts (1001 bytes), registry.ts (627 bytes) — no actual context caching or execution plan persistence implemented
runMission v11 flow is correct: Execution → Reflection (Worf) → Self-Correction loop (max 3) → Supabase storage → SUCCESS envelope
architecture_recommendations: Canonicalize run_factory_mission schema on context object shape across both servers (Phase 2)
Extract @sovereign/mcp-bridge package with personas.mjs as single source of truth (Phase 2, Step 3)
Extract @sovereign/crew-personas package re-exporting from mcp-bridge with MODEL_TIERS (Phase 2, Step 4)
Delete scripts/mcp-server.js and core/mcp-http-bridge.mjs after Phase 2 extraction
Implement VSCode context.ts: cache DDD context per session, invalidate on domain scaffold events
Fix Worf reflection parse: throw error on regex failure instead of defaulting to score 10
